messages:
maria (AE): Hey team — POC with EnvoyInc just started and theyre hitting mixed 429s and 401s from the Redwood API. Demo in ~30m. Can we spin up a quick war-room?

sam (Sales-Eng): On it, joining now. Can you paste the first failing request_id and a snippet of the response body?

jordan (EnvoyInc): Were seeing `invalid_api_key` and also occasional `rate_limit_exceeded`. We didnt change anything on our side. UI shows a bunch of failed generations.

oncall-bot: Deploy pipeline `prod/api` succeeded 12m ago :white_check_mark:

oliver (SRE): @maria @sam send me one `request_id` and `x-request-start` header from the failing request, Ill check the token-introspection path and rate limiter buckets.

maria (AE): Pasting a couple lines from their agent logs:```json
{"timestamp":"2026-02-18T14:02:10Z","request_id":"req_ab12","status":429,"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Token bucket depleted"}
{"timestamp":"2026-02-18T14:02:14Z","request_id":"req_ab13","status":401,"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Key not found"}
```

sam (Sales-Eng): Two hypotheses: (A) Their API key was rotated/disabled in the console, (B) our global quota saw a burst and consumed burst tokens. Quick checks: can you `curl -v` one failing request and paste response headers? Also tell me if they're on Shared Hosted or Dedicated for this POC.

jordan (EnvoyInc): Were on Hosted trial keys (self-provisioned via invite). Heres a curl dump from their environment:```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx-demo" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:02:14 GMT
X-Request-Id: req_ab13

{"error":{"code":"invalid_api_key","message":"Key not found"}}
```

jess (Sec): Tagging in — we rotated a subset of demo keys yesterday to expire compromised tokens. @jordan can you confirm which key string the EnvoyInc integration is using (last 6 chars)? Might be using an old key from the onboarding doc.

oliver (SRE): I pulled our auth logs for `req_ab12` / `req_ab13`. Observed pattern: token-introspect backend returned 502s from 14:01:50-14:03:00 (transient KMS upstream error), causing fallback to do a secondary lookup which then reported key-not-found for some tokens. Also saw a surge in requests from their org id consuming burst credits.

sam (Sales-Eng): OK plan for immediate remediation (30m demo):
1) @jordan create a fresh API key via Console -> API Keys (just for the demo).
2) If still getting 429 after new key, switch the demo to the dedicated fallback model (we can route their session to a reserved slot for 30m).
3) @oliver can you open a short-lived bypass for token-introspection circuit to avoid KMS flap?

jordan (EnvoyInc): I can create a new key now, but need exact scope to grant. What permissions does the demo need?

maria (AE): Needs generate + streaming. No admin. Sam, can you paste exact scope string? Ill relay.

sam (Sales-Eng): Use scope: `scope:generate,streaming`. In console click "Create key -> Demo" then copy full key and update their env var.

oliver (SRE): I kicked a config change to reduce token-introspect timeout from 5s -> 1s and enabled a short circuit to serve existing cached tokens while KMS recovers. Deploying now. If that holds, the `invalid_api_key` path shouldn't be triggered for valid cached keys.

oncall-bot: Rollout `auth/cache-circuit` started by oliver — 3 nodes remaining.

jordan (EnvoyInc): New key created and injected. Re-ran curl, now get:```json
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-Id: req_ab20
{"id":"gen_45","status":"queued"}
```

sam (Sales-Eng): Nice. Can you run a few full-generation flows to validate latency and consistency? If latency is high, we can temporarily route to Dedicated or lower model size.

jordan (EnvoyInc): Doing 5 runs now — 3/5 success, 2/5 timeouts ~12s. Anything else I should change?

oliver (SRE): Timeout spikes look like KV cache misses causing long-tail tokenization cost plus backend hotspot. Short-term: (A) we can throttle concurrency on their client to keep <= 6 reqs/sec, (B) we can route their API key to a reserved pool — I can assign them a 30-minute dedicated slot right now. Which do you prefer?
maria (AE): For the live demo I'd prefer reserved slot. Jordan, want us to spin that up?
jordan (EnvoyInc): Yes please, do reserved slot for the demo.

oliver (SRE): Done. Assigned `dedicated-poc-3` for 45 minutes, routing rule applied to their org id. You should see all requests hit the dedicated pool.

oncall-bot: Allocation `dedicated-poc-3` created (expires in 45m) by oliver.

jordan (EnvoyInc): Re-ran tests — 5/5 success, median latency 420ms. Demo green. Thank you!! :tada:

maria (AE): Amazing. Closing loop items:
- sam: document the quick-recover playbook (regen key + reserved slot + throttle) in the POC runbook.
- oliver: open an infra ticket to investigate KMS (token-introspect) flapping root cause.
- jess: confirm whether key rotations should have triggered customer notifications.

sam (Sales-Eng): Will update runbook + add a slide to the handoff doc with CLI commands:```bash
# quick new key via API (admin):
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.redwood.ai/admin/keys -d '{"label":"poc-temp","scopes":["generate","streaming"]}'
```

oliver (SRE): Ticket created: INF-2026-187 "KMS token-introspect transient 502s". Investigating circuit-breaker thresholds and cache TTLs.
jess (Sec): Ill follow up on rotation cadence and whether we need onboarding warnings for rotating demo keys.

maria (AE): Thanks all — I'll update the customer and mark the call as proceeding. If anything else pops up, re-open this thread. :pray:
